raw_segments.text: Mowgli stood upright the fire-pot in his hands. Then he stretched out his arms and yawned
in the face of the council. But he was furious with rage and sorrow, for wolf-like the wolves
had never told him how they hated him.
Listen, you, he cried. There is no need for this dog's jabber. You have told me so often
tonight that I am a man, and indeed I would have been a wolf with you to my life's end,
that I feel your words are true.
So I do not call you my brothers any more, but sag dogs, as a man should. What you will
do and what you will not do is not yours to say. That matter is with me, and that we may
